newsitem.title: USA: Fire still burning at PSE&G NJ substation.
newsitem.headline: Fire still burning at PSE&G NJ substation.

text.p: A fire at a Public Service Electric and Gas Co (PSE&G) substation in Elizabeth, New Jersey was still burning at 0915 EDT/1315 GMT, knocking out power to the city and parts of nearby Newark International airport, a company spokesman said.
"The fire is still burning. It has knocked out power to about 35,000 customers, including Newark airport," said company spokesman George Koodray.

Damage estimates to the Bayway substation were not immediately available. He said the cause of the fire, which broke out about 0530 EDT/0930 GMT, was not immediately known, though a local fire official told Reuters it appeared to have been caused by an exploding transformer.
"Right now our efforts are aimed at containing the fire," he said, adding that the utility was rerouting power to make conditions safer for firefighters at the blaze.
"We're rerouting power to pick up load elsewhere, but there's load you can't pick up at the substation. It wouldn't be safe for the firefighters," Koodray said.

"We're picking up a portion of the load at Newark airport through another substation, but capacity available through rerouting is not enough to pick up for the entire airport," he said, adding that parts of the airport are on backup generators.

A New Jersey State police officer said the fire forced police to close a nearby exit from the New Jersey Turnpike and knocked out power in parts of Elizabeth, a port city on the southwest side of New York harbor.
PSE&G, based in Newark, N.J., is a subsidiary of Public Service Enterprise Inc.
